missing_in_a: Publishing to arbitrary graph topics without preconfigured static routes
Runtime, client-supplied type resolution for topics/services
Latest-message whitelist configured via ROS parameters rather than static YAML file
missing_in_b: Hard request-size limit (413) and concurrent-connection admission with explicit 503 at cap
Config/route-count limits with distinct startup error/exit codes
Malformed-input resilience and timeout-leak (RSS) stress acceptance criteria
reasons: Both elaborate heavily beyond the one-line Thai prompt, but B's requirements pair every REQ with crisp Given/When/Then acceptance tests and its spec is self-contained (components, interfaces, data model, uniform error mapping) — implementable without chasing cross-references. A is gateway-faithful with a tight envelope and auth, but drowns in D-/F-/appendix citations to unseen documents, truncates mid-requirement, and pins many invented limits, harming readability and question-free implementability.
